correctness.rationale: The signed distance into the clockwise tangent at u is −H_u(v−u), obtained from Im[e^(−iu)(z(v)−z(u))], and H′_u=(u+w)sin w. For an earlier point, the v=0 value u−sin u and any earlier internal extrema are strictly positive, with zero only at v=u. For 0<T−u<2π the later minimum occurs at the contact test endpoint or at u; a full 2π turn instead gives H_u(2π)=−2π. The counterclockwise normal cannot support an interior regular point, because nearby points are strictly to the left of its tangent. Monotonic f(d)=(d−sin d)/(1−cos d) on (0,2π) then gives the unique terminal interval, as well as the unique first threshold α, the root of tan α=α in (π,3π/2), not the only positive root overall. At and below α every regular tangent supports the hull; continuity puts the cusp on its boundary. Beyond α, the tangent chord and all terminal tangents strictly separate earlier points. The terminal arc plus chord is the boundary of the terminal arc's hull (an injective boundary arc and its supporting chord); at T its normal cone is generated by the chord and final tangent normals, so earlier points also strictly satisfy every support inequality at that endpoint. Thus no earlier point adds a boundary piece. The full generating arc is still on the boundary at equality; strict exposure of its cusp is lost there, but the discarded interval is nonempty only above equality. Green's formula gives the signed comparison area and arc-length integration gives the perimeter. At contact f′(α)=ρ, yielding s=kη+O(η²) for η=T−α. Uniformly on 0≤v≤s the gap is (ρ+1)(v−kη)+O(η²) and J=ρ+1+O(η). Integrating −vH/2 and v[J/√(J²+H²)−1] gives respectively (ρ+1)k³η³/12 and −k⁴η⁴/24. The contact branch is analytic and the nonzero leading defects give the stated differentiability. Expanding f(2π−u)=4π/u²+π/3+O(u) gives the one-turn limit with the stated error. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed. Its output counts 44 diagnostics, but the tightest perimeter ratio is printed without an assertion (43 assertions in that run); this does not affect the analytical result.

value.rationale: The first loss of a prefix of a classical, continuously truncated curve is a natural convex-hull problem. The exact contact equation identifies the entire surviving arc for any truncation, not just near threshold or for point samples. The positive cubic signed-area defect and negative quartic perimeter defect detect the same event with different differentiability orders; their sharp constants and the long-window asymptotic are directly usable, without a claim of a general spiral law.
